events.credibility_reason: Self-styled proof of the twin prime conjecture on a non-reviewed platform via an elementary 'factorial-based primality criterion', a method the problem is known to resist; a reader comment identifies a failure point; no uptake. Irrelevant to balanced primes in any case.
Self-published Zenodo claims to prove Polignac's conjecture, with many rapid revisions, partly numerical, no uptake on a landmark problem.

why: The statement asks only whether infinitely many balanced primes exist. No event bears on that unconditionally. Eismann restates it, Rocchelli's OEIS conjectures assume infinitude, and the Weisenberg and Abel forum posts reduce it to the open Hypothesis H (a folklore conditional implication). None of these settles or bounds anything, so all are scope none. Batalov's record CPAP-3 is one finite instance, dated 2023, so it is before the snapshot. The prime-gap results (bounded gaps 236 and 186, large gaps) and the twin-prime and Polignac claims answer different questions, so they are variant. The Axiom Lean work formalises a known result, so it is none. The two crank-style twin-prime and Polignac claims are also not_credible. The OpenAI events have empty ai.systems with none_found false, so their AI role is none here. They are variant anyway.
doubts: The OpenAI large-gaps event is dated only '2026', but that year is wholly after 26 Jan 2024, so it is placed after the snapshot. Whether AI produced the OpenAI prime-gap mathematics is unresolved in the record, but it does not matter for this problem.
